record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: In Pb–Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV, ALICE measured inclusive J/ψ polarization with respect to an axis perpendicular to the event plane, using the spin-density-matrix element ρ00 or the related λθ parameter to probe effects from early electromagnetic fields and/or QGP vorticity. What theoretical description can quantitatively connect the observed small but significant λθ > 0 polarization effect to the underlying QGP properties, and can future D*+ vector-meson polarization measurements determine the charm spin alignment generated at the earliest stages of the collision and transferred through hadronisation?

evidence.quote: By measuring the polarisation with respect to the estimated reaction plane of the nuclear collision one selects a reference frame that should naturally be connected with the observation of polarisation effects due to the presence of early electromagnetic fields and/or QGP vorticity.
A small but significant polarisation effect (λθ > 0), reaching 3.9σ for 2 < pT < 4 GeV/c and 30–50% centrality, is measured.

However, a solid interpretation of the result that would allow a quantitative understanding of this observation and a precise connection with the QGP properties at its origin requires dedicated theory studies, which unfortunately are not yet available in the field.

From the experimental side, future polarisation studies should be performed using the D*+ vector meson, which could bring additional information about the charm spin alignment expected at the very early stages of heavy-ion collisions due to the produced magnetic field, transferred to the D*+ mesons via the hadronisation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider ultra-relativistic Pb–Pb collisions at a nucleon–nucleon center-of-mass energy √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, in which a quark–gluon plasma (QGP) is produced together with strong, short-lived electromagnetic fields and a large fluid vorticity associated with the angular momentum of the non-central collision. For an inclusive sample of J/ψ mesons reconstructed at forward rapidity, define the polarization with respect to an axis perpendicular to the reaction (event) plane via the angular distribution of the positive-charge decay lepton in the J/ψ rest frame,

  dN/d cos θ ∝ 1 + λ_θ cos² θ,

equivalently parametrized by the spin-density-matrix element ρ_{00} = (1 − λ_θ)/(3 + λ_θ). In the kinematic window 2 < p_T < 4 GeV/c and centrality class 30–50%, a small but statistically significant positive value λ_θ > 0 is observed.

(a) Construct a quantitative theoretical framework that connects this measured λ_θ(p_T, centrality) to the underlying QGP properties—specifically, to the magnitude and time evolution of the early-stage electromagnetic field, to the local fluid vorticity field ω^μ(x), and to the modification of the cc̄ bound-state dynamics in the deconfined medium—and that reproduces the observed sign, magnitude, and p_T-/centrality-dependence of λ_θ.

(b) Determine, within such a framework, the predicted polarization (λ_θ or ρ_{00}) of the D*+ vector meson in the same collision system, accounting for the spin alignment of the charm quark generated at the earliest stages of the collision by the produced magnetic field and for the spin transfer through hadronization to the D*+ final state. Specify whether the predicted D*+ polarization signal is large enough to be experimentally distinguishable from zero and from charmonium polarization, and identify the observables that would isolate the early-time charm-spin-alignment contribution from later medium effects.
artifact.status_search_result: The ALICE measurement of inclusive J/ψ polarization with respect to the event plane in Pb–Pb at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV established a small but significant λ_θ > 0 effect, but a fully quantitative theoretical description connecting it to QGP electromagnetic fields and vorticity is not yet established. Recent theoretical work (e.g., dissociation-driven quarkonium spin alignment, 2025) proposes mechanisms but does not yet provide a complete quantitative match. D*+ polarization measurements in Pb–Pb have not yet been reported. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Dissociation-driven quarkonium spin alignment in Pb–Pb collisions at √s_NN=5.02 TeV
status_evidence.snippet: effective Hamiltonian with a medium-modified color-singlet potential gives rise to spin-dependent dissociation, a plausible mechanism contributing to quarkonium spin alignment
status_evidence.claim: Recent theory proposes a dissociation-based mechanism for quarkonium spin alignment but a fully quantitative connection to ALICE data is still being developed.

status_evidence.title: J/ψ polarization in relativistic heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: theoretical study of J/psi polarization in heavy-ion collisions linking spin alignment to medium magnetic field and vorticity
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical investigations of the ALICE polarization observation are ongoing and not yet conclusive.

status_evidence.title: ALICE J/ψ polarization w.r.t. event plane (HEPData)
status_evidence.snippet: Measurement of the J/psi polarization with respect to the event plane in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC
status_evidence.claim: The experimental λ_θ > 0 result is established; the quantitative theoretical interpretation remains pending.
